change.author: Sam Jewell

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path, so the feature-flag check does nothing
findings.body: Both branches return `false`, so the `IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` call (line 195) has no effect, and the inverted `enabled := !...` name points the wrong way. Turning on `sqlExpressions` still gives "sqlExpressions is not implemented", which is what the PR wants. But a reader will take this for a flag gate with a bug in it. Either drop the helper and return the error directly in `case QueryTypeSQL` (with a comment saying SQL expressions are disabled until a new engine lands), or write it as `return false // disabled: no SQL engine`.

findings.title: The legacy node path is not gated and reports a misleading 'invalid sql' error
findings.body: Only `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` checks `enableSqlExpressions`. The legacy `TypeSQL` branch in `pkg/expr/nodes.go:159-160` calls `UnmarshalSQLCommand` → `NewSQLCommand` → `sql.TablesList`, which now always fails because the stub `RunCommands` returns "not implemented". The user gets the BadRequest `sql-invalid-sql` / "error reading SQL command", and a Warn "invalid sql query" is logged, which suggests their SQL is malformed. Consider returning the same "sqlExpressions is not implemented" error early in `NewSQLCommand` or `UnmarshalSQLCommand`, so both paths fail the same way and the message is accurate.

findings.title: DB.TablesList stub is unused
findings.body: Nothing calls the `TablesList` method on `DB`. The only callers use the package-level `sql.TablesList` (`pkg/expr/sql_command.go:30`, `pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go`), and that function goes through `RunCommands`. The method sits next to the package function of the same name, which is confusing. Remove it unless a planned interface needs it.

contracts.action: Parsing a query with type "sql" via ExpressionQueryReader now always returns an error
contracts.equivalent_path: Legacy TypeSQL branch in buildCMDNode: pkg/expr/nodes.go:159-160 → UnmarshalSQLCommand → NewSQLCommand
contracts.before_after: Before: with the flag on, it read the SQLExpression and built an SQLCommand through go-duck. After: the reader fails with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' whatever the flag says. The legacy path is not gated; it fails inside NewSQLCommand because the stub RunCommands errors, which gives BadRequest 'error reading SQL command'.
contracts.visible_effect: Any SQL expression in a query or alert returns an error. The message depends on which path parsed it.
contracts.failure_mode: Fails loudly in both paths. Nothing fails silently: Execute is never reached because the command cannot be built.

contracts.before_after: Before: ran the SQL in DuckDB. After: always returns 'not implemented', which ends up in rsp.Error.
contracts.visible_effect: Not reachable in practice, because NewSQLCommand fails first. If it were reached, the error would show in the result.
contracts.failure_mode: The error is put in rsp.Error and logged.

summary: The PR removes the go-duck dependency and puts not-implemented stubs in its place, which turns SQL expressions off. It does that, and both parse paths fail loudly rather than silently. Three things to consider: `enableSqlExpressions` returns false on every path, so its feature-flag check does nothing; the legacy nodes.go path is not gated and fails with a misleading 'error reading SQL command' / 'invalid sql query'; and the unused `DB.TablesList` stub has the same name as the package-level `TablesList`.
